les: Van die Limpopo tot oor die Indiese Oseaan
kaps_punt: Mapungubwe: eerste staat in Suider-Afrika 1220 - 1300: Handel regoor Afrika en die Indiese Oseaan en verder (globalisering); Goedere waarmee handel gedryf is

items.bewering: Jy ruil dalk by die skool 'n toebroodjie vir vrugte. Handel werk op dieselfde manier tussen plekke wat ver van mekaar lê.
items.bron: Mapping checked against dictionary definitions of barter and trade (Wordsmyth/American Heritage via Wordnik: 'trading goods or services without exchanging money'; Britannica Dictionary, britannica.com/dictionary/trade). The mapping (one good handed over for another) holds. Where a learner might over-extend it is to imagine Mapungubwe people swapping face to face with the people overseas, but the lesson closes that itself in 'Die pad na die see' (goods passed from trader to trader) and 'Een wêreld' (the two ends never knew each other). No false inference is left standing.

items.bewering: Handel is wanneer mense goedere of dienste uitruil: deur te ruil, of deur te koop en te verkoop.
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary, 'trade': the activity or process of buying, selling, or exchanging goods or services (https://www.britannica.com/dictionary/trade); Dictionary.com notes trade includes exchange without money.

items.bewering: In Mapungubwe se tyd het die mense van die vallei nie geld soos ons s'n gebruik nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Kingdom of Mapungubwe (citing Chirikure et al. 2015 p. 22; Huffman 2005 pp. 52-3): imported glass beads were 'used as currency', and tribute was paid in crops and animals. No coins or notes are known from Mapungubwe. The sentence is hedged 'geld soos ons s'n', which stays true even under the beads-as-currency reading. Note for a human, not a fault: the same scholarship that supports this also describes beads functioning like money, so the claim should not be hardened to 'they had no money at all'.

items.bewering: Mense het toe goed vir ander goed geruil en ons noem dit ruilhandel.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Kingdom of Mapungubwe (Huffman 2005): ivory, gold and skins traded for glass beads, cloth and glazed ceramics, which is goods for goods; barter definitions as in item 1 (Wordnik/American Heritage).

items.bewering: Goud en ivoor het uit die Limpopo-vallei na die kus weggegaan.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Kingdom of Mapungubwe: 'Mapungubwe exported gold and ivory' (Chirikure et al. 2015 p. 22; Huffman 2005 pp. 52-3); EBSCO Research Starters, Mapungubwe: traded 'gold and ivory to the international markets on Indian Ocean networks'; Coutu and Sealy (tDAR 431936) on ivory feeding the Indian Ocean trade. Nuance, not a fault: the gold was mostly not mined in the valley. It likely came from the Tati goldfields and south-western Zimbabwe (Wikipedia, citing Chirikure et al. 2015), and EBSCO says the rulers taxed it 'as it passed through the region'. The sentence says the gold left the valley, which is true.

items.bewering: Ivoor kom van 'n olifant se lang tande. Dit is hard en wit en mense kon dit in mooi vorms kerf.
items.bron: Britannica, 'ivory': a variety of dentin of which the elephant's tusk (an upper incisor tooth) is composed, 'prized for its beauty, durability, and suitability for carving' (https://www.britannica.com/print/article/298285). Colour is creamy white, which is fair to call 'wit' at this level. Coutu et al. 2016 (doi 10.1007/s10437-016-9232-0) and Coutu and Sealy 2017 (tDAR 431936) found that worked southern African Iron Age ivory was elephant. Carved ivory (bracelets) was made at Mapungubwe (Wikipedia, citing Antonites 2019).

items.bewering: Glasperle en lap het van ver oorkant die see na die vallei gekom.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Kingdom of Mapungubwe (Huffman 2005): glass beads, cotton and silk cloth received in return; glass beads came from India and Southeast Asia. M. Wood, Interconnections (Uppsala, 2011): LA-ICP-MS shows the southern African bead series largely originated in South or Southeast Asia. Whitelaw, The Digging Stick April 2024 (archaeology.org.za): Limpopo valley sites received 'glass beads and probably cloth' (via search summary; the PDF itself did not extract). Imported cloth does not survive archaeologically and is inferred, but the inference is standard.

items.bewering: Glasperle is klein perle van glas, en die glas self is nie in die vallei gemaak nie.
items.bron: Wood 2011 (chemical origin in South/Southeast Asia); University of Pretoria research article 'On the edges of Mapungubwe's influence' (via search summary): the beads were imported rather than made locally. The wording 'die glas self' is correctly careful: K2 did make large 'garden roller' beads locally by re-melting imported beads (Wikipedia, citing Wingfield et al. 2020 p. 163; Loubser 1991), so 'the beads were not made in the valley' would be too strong. 'The glass was not made in the valley' is true. Writers should not 'tidy' this into the stronger form.

items.bewering: Hierdie lap is geweefde stof.
items.bron: Definitional. Cloth is woven fabric; the imported goods named in the literature are cotton and silk cloth (Wikipedia, Kingdom of Mapungubwe, Huffman 2005).

items.bewering: Mense het van daardie glasperle later by Mapungubwe uit die grond gegrawe. Daardie perle is vandag ons getuienis dat die handel werklik gebeur het.
items.bron: University of Pretoria Mapungubwe Collection (excavated material from K2 and Mapungubwe, including trade glass beads; via search summary of up.ac.za and repository.up.ac.za); UP research article: a royal hilltop grave held more than 24 000 glass beads, which researchers treat as evidence of the trade network because they were imported.

items.bewering: Die pad uit die vallei het eers oor land na die ooskus van Afrika geloop.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Kingdom of Mapungubwe: 'Though not navigable itself, traders followed the Limpopo River inland' (Chirikure et al. 2015 p. 20), so the journey was overland along the river. The coastal ports were Chibuene, later Sofala (Chirikure et al. 2015 pp. 25-6). EBSCO Research Starters names Chibuene as the port that grew on this trade.

items.bewering: Die goed het van die een handelaar na die volgende oorgegaan. Ander handelaars by die see het dit met skepe oor die Indiese Oseaan na ver plekke geneem.
items.bron: EBSCO Research Starters, Mapungubwe: ivory went 'for export to the coast, from where Swahili merchants transported it into the wider world'. WorldHistory.org, Mapungubwe: coastal states 'traded with merchants travelling from India and Arabia by sea'. Search summaries of the Met essay (metmuseum.org, which returned 429 when opened directly) and other sources: goods went via Chibuene and on by Swahili dhows to Kilwa and beyond. The sentence does not claim coastal traders never came inland (Huffman reads the palace celadon as a gift for permission to trade), so it stands either way.

items.bewering: Handelaars het hierdie pad gereeld gevolg en ons noem dit 'n handelsroete. / 'n Handelsroete is die pad wat handelaars gereeld volg om goedere van die een plek na die ander te neem.
items.bron: Standard meaning of 'trade route' (an established route regularly used by traders to carry goods), consistent with dictionary usage. A repeated route to Chibuene/Sofala over several centuries is documented (Chirikure et al. 2015 via Wikipedia).

items.bewering: Iemand ver oorkant die see het die glas vir daardie perle gemaak. Iemand in die Limpopo-vallei het dieselfde perle gedra.
items.bron: Wood 2011, Interconnections: South/Southeast Asian origin of the glass; Wikipedia (Huffman 2005): beads from India and Southeast Asia. Beads were worn and buried with the dead at Mapungubwe (UP royal grave, more than 24 000 beads; WorldHistory.org).

items.bewering: Goud uit die vallei het ook ver oorkant die see beland.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Kingdom of Mapungubwe: gold and ivory went to the Indian Ocean trade via Sofala (Huffman 2005 pp. 38-51), and Sofala was frequented by Arab merchants because of rising demand for gold (Chirikure et al. 2015 pp. 25-6). As with the gold item in 'Wat weggegaan het', 'uit die vallei' is true as 'out of the valley'. The gold was largely mined further north and passed through; the lesson does not say it was mined in the valley.

items.bewering: Daardie mense het mekaar nie geken nie en tog was hulle aan mekaar verbind. Dit was dus nie twee aparte wêreldjies nie maar een wêreld.
items.bron: Mapping checked. The metaphor 'one world, not two little worlds' stands for connection through a chain of trade. That fits the literature: Wood 2011 concludes southern Africa was integrated into Eurasian and African trade cycles, and EBSCO and the Met (via search summary) describe the Swahili traders as only indirectly involved. 'Did not know each other' refers to the bead-maker and the wearer, which is certainly true across a multi-stage chain. Where it could over-reach: a learner might think the two places were as tightly bound as today's world. Nothing in the text says so, and the begrip below defines the term modestly. Not a fault.

items.bewering: Vandag noem ons so 'n verbinding tussen ver plekke globalisering. / Globalisering is wanneer plekke ver van mekaar deel van een wêreld word.
items.bron: Lancaster University psychology glossary: globalisation is 'the highly uneven but increasing interconnection of the different parts of the world'; Giddens' sociological definition is the intensification of worldwide social relations linking distant localities (via search summary); Oxford Learner's Dictionaries: cultures and economies around the world becoming connected. The begrip is a simplification of 'distant places becoming interconnected' and does not cross into falsehood. Applying the term to Mapungubwe is the CAPS heading's own framing.

items.bewering: Die koning en die leiers het baie meer glasperle van oorkant die see gehad as gewone mense.
items.blok: Die koning en die skaars goed
items.bron: UP research article (via search summary): a royal hilltop grave held more than 24 000 glass beads, and beads also turned up at small family sites away from the capital. That fits 'baie meer', which does not claim commoners had none. WorldHistory.org: the king 'owned more cattle and precious materials acquired via trade than anyone else'. Met essay (via search summary): elaborate elite burials with exotic glass beads, contrasted with commoners at the foot of the hill. This is a comparative, not a superlative; no superlative occurs in the lesson text.

items.bewering: Dit was skaars goed wat van baie ver af gekom het.
items.blok: Die koning en die skaars goed
items.bron: UCT thesis 'Glass beads as indicators of contact and trade in Southern Africa ca. AD 900-1250' (open.uct.ac.za/handle/11427/19418): glass beads were very rare and increased only with Indian Ocean trade. Wikipedia (Loubser 1991): beads were fused into 'garden rollers' to raise their value and prestige. Origin in South/Southeast Asia: Wood 2011.

items.bewering: Die handel het die koning al ryker gemaak. Sy groter rykdom het hom ook al magtiger gemaak.
items.blok: Die koning en die skaars goed
items.bron: Wikipedia, Kingdom of Mapungubwe: the Indian Ocean trade generated 'the large amount of wealth' that created unprecedented inequalities (Huffman 2005 p. 30). WorldHistory.org: trade prosperity 'would likely have led to a strengthening of political authority', with a central authority that monopolised trade. EBSCO Research Starters: the chief had the privilege of collecting half of the profit from luxury trade, and power rested on wealth. Scholars also stress tribute, cattle and coercion as sources of power (Chirikure et al. 2015 p. 92). The lesson says trade made him richer and more powerful, not that trade alone did, so it stays true.

items.bewering: Ruilhandel is wanneer mense goedere of dienste direk vir mekaar ruil sonder geld.
items.bron: Wordsmyth and American Heritage (via Wordnik): barter is trading goods or services directly without money; Vocabulary.com, 'barter'.

items.bewering: Ivoor is die harde wit materiaal van 'n olifant se tande.
items.bron: Britannica, 'ivory': 'a variety of dentin of which the tusk of the elephant is composed'. Hippopotamus, walrus and narwhal teeth are also recognised as ivory but are commercially minor. Read alone, the entry names the main source and does not exclude the others, and the ivory traded from these sites was elephant (Coutu and Sealy 2017). An acceptable simplification rather than a false definition.

items.bewering: Handel is wanneer mense goedere of dienste uitruil: deur te ruil, of deur te koop en te verkoop.
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary, 'trade' (https://www.britannica.com/dictionary/trade). Identical wording to the study-text sentence in 'Ruil sonder geld'.

opsomming: All 23 claims hold and the lesson text has no superlative ('eerste staat' sits only in the copied CAPS heading); two careful phrasings must not be 'tidied', because they are true only as worded: 'die glas self is nie in die vallei gemaak nie' (K2 re-melted imported beads) and 'geld soos ons s'n' (some scholars say glass beads served as currency).
